nfl.oneThing: Jacoby Brissett is heading to Baltimore from Arizona, with the NFL trade deadline on 10 November.

headlines.title: Ravens get Brissett from Arizona before the deadline
headlines.summary: The Ravens are acquiring quarterback Jacoby Brissett from Arizona, sources told ESPN and NFL Network. Baltimore gives up a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 seventh-round pick, and gets a 2027 fifth-round pick back in the deal. Arizona receives undisclosed draft compensation. Lamar Jackson is out after right thumb surgery, and Joe Fagnano threw two interceptions in Baltimore's 33–10 loss to Jacksonville. The Ravens are 4–5 and on a four-game losing streak.
headlines.whyItMatters: Baltimore sits 1.5 games behind the last AFC playoff spot, so a quarterback change matters with the deadline on 10 November.

headlines.title: Patriots’ Henderson dealing with neurological symptoms
headlines.summary: Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson says tests have come back positive after he suffered “unexplained neurological symptoms” that remain “unknown and unexplainable.” New England has ruled him out for Sunday, along with wide receiver A.J. Brown, who is out with a knee injury. Coach Mike Vrabel says the focus is on supporting Henderson through the medical issue. The Patriots host the Packers on Sunday, and they are 5–3 and seventh in the AFC.
headlines.whyItMatters: New England's 5–3 start has them in the AFC playoff picture, so the absences matter as well as Henderson's health.

headlines.title: Eagles start Milton as Giants lean on Singletary
headlines.summary: Giants running back Cam Skattebo is officially doubtful for Sunday at Philadelphia with a hamstring injury, after missing a fourth straight practice. Coach John Harbaugh says the Giants have not ruled him out. If he can't play, Devin Singletary is expected to be the lead back. For the Eagles, Joe Milton makes his first start at quarterback. DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out for a third straight game, and Tanner McKee is questionable with a rib injury. Philadelphia is 2–6 after six straight losses.
headlines.whyItMatters: The Giants are 4–2–1 and third in the NFC. The Eagles' six-game losing streak puts pressure on Milton's first start.

teamNews.title: Darien Porter questionable with a groin injury
teamNews.text: Darien Porter is questionable for Sunday at San Francisco. He hurt his groin on the first defensive play of the 38–33 win at the Jets and didn't practise Wednesday, but worked Thursday and Friday. If he can't play, rookies Jermod McCoy and Zeke Masses will rotate as they did in Week 8.

contextCard.title: How the NFL trade deadline works
contextCard.body: Teams can trade players and draft picks until the deadline, which is 10 November this season. Once it passes, trades stop until the off-season. Draft picks are the usual currency in these deals. The Ravens' move for Jacoby Brissett, for example, cost a fourth-round and a seventh-round pick.

headlines.title: Wembanyama scores a career-high 52 in Spurs win
headlines.summary: Victor Wembanyama had a career night with 52 points, 24 rebounds and 8 blocks as the Spurs beat the Mavericks 112–111. Kyrie Irving had a chance to win it late but missed, a moment former Mavericks coach Jason Kidd has since reacted to. Shaq said of Wembanyama, “We’ve never seen a player like him.” The win was San Antonio's sixth straight, and the Spurs are 6–2 and fifth in the West.
headlines.whyItMatters: Wembanyama leads the league in blocks at 4.5 a game and is fourth in scoring at 29.0 points. The Spurs go to Sacramento on Friday with a chance to keep the streak alive.

headlines.title: Philadelphia’s 8–1 start draws superteam talk
headlines.summary: The 76ers are 8–1, the best record in the East, and have won five straight. Brian Windhorst and Tim MacMahon say league insiders are seeing early superteam signs in Philadelphia. Their column also looks at Memphis, who are 6–2 and have held up well. Bleacher Report's power rankings feature LeBron James' 76ers and the rising Spurs.
headlines.whyItMatters: Philadelphia sits first in the East, ahead of Detroit and Boston, who are both 6–2. Early form like this sets the tone for the playoff race.

headlines.title: Giannis skips media after Heat loss, Rivers weighs in
headlines.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo skipped his media availability after the Heat lost 120–100 at Golden State. Former Bucks coach Doc Rivers says Giannis “didn't want to be the bad guy” when he sought a trade out of Milwaukee last season. Rivers also says Giannis has “one way: downhill, force, force.” The Bucks are 1–7 on a four-game losing streak.
headlines.whyItMatters: Milwaukee are 15th in the East, and the Heat are 3–6 and 10th. The off-court noise comes on top of a difficult start.
